violations.why: closer1_isr (higher priority) can preempt writer1_isr between its write and read of array[9000] and overwrite it, so the read sees 999 instead of 1.
closer1_isr can preempt closer2_isr between its two reads of test_global_var1 in JudgeCondi, so the two reads can see different values.
closer1_isr can preempt closer2_isr, which has just written tco_write_buf. Its own write to the same buffer means the later read at line 429 may not see the 'V' that closer2 wrote.
Closer1 and closer2 have equal priority and can preempt each other, so closer2 can overwrite the buffer between closer1's write and its read.
closer1_isr can preempt closer2_isr between its write of 42 and the check on the next line, and change tco_expect_close (e.g. to 0 via release). The check can then fail.
closer2_isr can preempt closer1_isr between its write of 42 and the reset in release. It then reads an intermediate value that is not what a serial execution would produce.
